details: CONFIRMED by reading. The reword added a test but kept the older, wider list beside it; "state" is the one example that

queue item. "logs" is fine (gate-log lines are repeated). Size: 5 min.

rules/structured-data.md:7  "- What counts as read by a script: state, verdicts, items, logs, votes. Each is a structured"
rules/front.md:6            "up to date (state, decisions and who made them, the owner's latest"
failing_case: A reviewer carrying this rule meets docs/handover.md: it holds "state, decisions ..." (rules/front.md:6) and a later step
(the front after compaction) reads it. Line 7 says "What counts as read by a script: state, verdicts, items, logs, votes.
Each is a structured file" with no condition, so the reviewer flags the handover as prose-that-must-be-JSON. Line 4-6 (the
new test) says the opposite: a single record, not one of many of the same shape, stays prose. Two answers for one file;
the owner's words were "store ONLY structured data that can be splitted into repeated domain data".
fix_hint: Fold line 7 into the test: "What counts: queue items, verdicts, ledger lines, log lines, votes: each a structured file, not
prose with labels." (drop "state"), or condition it ("state kept as repeated records").

- It still gives "structured file" for queue items, verdicts, ledger lines, votes (repeated records a script reads).
- It still gives "structured file" for gate-log lines (gate-log-summary queue item), which are repeated records.
- The bullet listing what counts no longer names a kind of data that is not a repeated record (no bare "state").

details: CONFIRMED by reading; correct for a careful reader who also reads the body, unclear for one who sees only the gist. Size: 5 min.
evidence: lib/relay_rules.py:40 takes lines[1] as "gist"; render_target lists title + gist for rules not loaded in full.
failing_case: The gist is the only line most sessions see (relay sync puts it under "Rules to read when they apply" in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md).
It reads "... is stored as a structured file (JSON, TOML or YAML) with a schema check, and changed only through one script,
when it is one of many records of the same shape; ...". Read as written, the condition qualifies the last clause: everything
a later step reads is stored structured, and only repeated records need one writer. That reverses the owner's decision.
fix_hint: Move the condition forward: "Information that a script, a hook or a later step reads, when it is one of many records of the
same shape, is stored as a structured file ... and changed only through one script; instructions and prose stay text."
pass_cases: - The gist, read alone, says the condition (one of many records of the same shape) decides whether data is stored structured.
- The gist still starts "Information that a script, a hook or a later step reads is stored as a structured file" or the test
at tests/test_queue.py:1087 is updated with it.
- The gist still names instructions and prose as staying text.
reason: Gist line 2 puts the condition before "is stored as a structured file"; tests/test_queue.py:1087 asserts it.
findings.summary: in the gist, 'when it is one of many records' attaches to 'changed only through one script', not to 'is stored as a structured file'

details: CONFIRMED by reading; no code reads this word, so correct today, unclear. Size: 5 min.
evidence: rules/structured-data.md:6 "briefs, reports and hand-backs are text for people and models and stay prose."
failing_case: Line 6 lists "reports" among texts that stay prose. In relay a review report is a JSON file of [[finding]] records written by
`relay check record review` (the judge base: "Your output is one report, stored as a JSON file"). A reader of the rule alone
can conclude review reports should be prose; the intended meaning is agent reports for people (scout, fixer reports).
fix_hint: "agent reports" or "fixer and scout reports" instead of "reports".
pass_cases: - The rule names which reports stay prose (agent reports read by a person or a model) so review/check reports (repeated
findings, verdicts) are plainly on the structured side.
- Hand-backs, briefs, rules, instructions still stay prose.
reason: Line 6 says "agent reports", and a verdict is one structured record; tests/test_queue.py:1096.
findings.summary: 'reports ... stay prose' collides with review reports, which relay stores as JSON findings
